_comment: What the desk tells a scribe about their own tools. Content, not code: this is the copy that answers 'what does this button do', and it should be editable without touching the UI. It describes CONTROLS ONLY — never goals. Nothing here may say what documenting a road is worth, or that finishing one does anything at all: docs/design/playtest-script.md §2 measures whether a player finds that out unprompted, and a sentence in this file would end that measurement for every session afterwards. Costs are not written here either — the UI reads those off sim constants so they cannot rot.
entry_note: A quick hand: whatever the road has just shown you.
entry_record: Prices, names, who deals with whom. Longer, and worth the ink.
entry_survey: A full description of the leg of road behind you — the stretch you have walked to get here, not the place you are standing in.
entry_treatise: A considered piece, written at length. The most a scribe can spend on one entry.
writing: Every entry costs daylight and something to write on. Nothing you learn survives you unless it is written and reaches the archive.
media: Clay and papyrus are what you write on. Clay is cheap and heavy and survives water; papyrus is light and cheap to carry and does not. Running out ends the writing, not the season.
seals: A sealed entry is authoritative. Unsealed work still reaches the archive, but as rumour, and rumour is worth half.
seal_toggle_off: Unsealed — the next entry reaches the archive as rumour.
seal_toggle_on: Sealed — the next entry is authoritative, and spends a seal.
courier: Sends a copy of the ledger home now, ahead of you. What is sent survives you; what you write afterwards does not.
contracts: Signed at a settlement that offers them, and written down like everything else. They pay while you travel, and are called in when the road turns against you.
archive: What the House has in writing. It is all that crosses from one scribe to the next.
empty_pack: Nothing left to write on. The road home still has to be walked.
